article_title: ESLint Adds an Official Shell Script Linting Plugin, Extending Its Language-Agnostic Platform
summary: Automated check only flagged an allowlist warning, but manual source-by-source verification found a pattern of quote-fidelity failures in the body — including one fully fabricated direct quote attributed to the mvdan/sh GitHub repository that does not appear anywhere in that page — which a single corrections note cannot honestly cover. Chief Editor overrides the script's APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to REJECT.

findings.details:
eslint.org: https://eslint.org/blog/2026/11/eslint-shell-plugin-announcement/
shellcheck.net: https://www.shellcheck.net/ — both independently confirmed by the Chief Editor as official/canonical sites (eslint.org is ESLint's own blog, linked from the ESLint GitHub org; shellcheck.net is ShellCheck's own official site, linked from the koalaman/shellcheck GitHub repo and cited by name in both the ESLint announcement and the eslint/shell README) and added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review's commit. This finding alone would not have blocked approval.

findings.message: Fabricated direct quote attributed to the mvdan/sh GitHub repository
findings.details: Article body states: 'shfmt is "the formatting utility bundled with this project," used to standardize shell script formatting' and cites https://github.com/mvdan/sh. This exact phrase does not appear anywhere in the snapshot (sources/2026-11/eslint-adds-an-official-shell-script-linting-plugin-extending-its-language-agnostic-platform/source-2.html.gz) — verified by grep -io 'bundled' and grep -io "formatting utility" against the decompressed HTML, both zero hits. The repository's actual language is 'A shell parser, formatter, and interpreter with bash and zsh support; includes shfmt' (About line) and 'shfmt formats shell programs' (README). The underlying fact (shfmt is a formatting tool included in the mvdan/sh project) is true, but the quoted wording was invented, not lifted from the source.

findings.message: Additional quote-fidelity issues in the body (pattern, not isolated)
findings.details: 1) Quote 'a set of rules inspired by ShellCheck checks, and a recommended configuration' is attributed to the eslint.org announcement (source-0), but that exact wording ('ShellCheck checks') only appears in the eslint/shell GitHub README (source-1); the blog post itself reads '...inspired by ShellCheck, and a recommended configuration' (no 'checks'). Misattributed to the wrong cited source. 2) Quote 'enables rules catching common problems, such as unquoted expansions, unused variables, and unsafe read usage' alters the announcement's actual text, 'enables rules that catch common problems, such as unquoted expansions, unused variables, and unsafe read usage.' 3) Quote 'cover[s] issues including legacy command substitutions, iterating over ls output, unquoted expansions, and variables in printf format strings' substitutes 'including' for the source's actual 'such as' ('Its rules cover issues such as legacy command substitutions...') without marking the substitution. 4) The closing quote 'Shell scripts are an important part of many projects. With @eslint/shell, users can lint shell scripts alongside other code using ESLint's configuration system' alters the announcement's actual closing text: 'Shell scripts are an important part of many projects, from build and release automation to local development tools. With @eslint/shell, you can lint shell scripts alongside the rest of your code using ESLint's configuration system and familiar rule APIs.' ('you'->'users', 'the rest of your code'->'other code', drops 'and familiar rule APIs', truncates the first sentence without an ellipsis).

content_preview.title: ESLint Adds an Official Shell Script Linting Plugin, Extending Its Language-Agnostic Platform
content_preview.summary: ESLint introduced @eslint/shell, an officially supported plugin that lints Bash, POSIX sh and mksh scripts with rules inspired by ShellCheck.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

ESLint now officially supports linting shell scripts. According to [ESLint's announcement](https://eslint.org/blog/2026/11/eslint-shell-plugin-announcement/), the project introduced the `@eslint/shell` plugin on November 6, giving the JavaScript-ecosystem linter the ability to check Bash, POSIX `sh` and MirBSD Korn shell (mksh) scripts alongside the JavaScript, JSON, Markdown and CSS files it already handles.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News article (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters), 601 words (within the News 400-1200 range), neutral and professional tone, no AI self-reference, no sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources snapshotted successfully (status 200, no suspicious_patterns) and read in full from the gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-11/eslint-adds-an-official-shell-script-linting-plugin-extending-its-language-agnostic-platform/ after re-hashing each decompressed file against manifest.json sha256 values (all matched): source-0.html.gz (eslint.org blog announcement) — read in full; confirms publish date Nov 6, 2026, the July 2024 general-purpose-linter plan, prior JSON/Markdown/CSS support, Bash/POSIX/mksh support, ESTree-style tree, mvdan-sh/shfmt parser basis, and the closing statement (with the alteration noted in findings). source-1.html.gz (github.com/eslint/shell README) — read in full; confirms npm install command, Node ^20.19.0||^22.13.0||>=24, tested with ESLint v10, Apache-2.0 license, shell/bash|posix|mksh language names, and is the actual source of the verbatim 'ShellCheck checks' phrase the article misattributes to the blog. source-2.html.gz (github.com/mvdan/sh) — read in full, plus targeted grep for 'bundled' and 'formatting utility' (zero hits in both); confirms 'A shell parser, formatter, and interpreter' and POSIX/Bash/Zsh/mksh support, but does NOT contain the quote the article attributes to it regarding shfmt. source-3.html.gz (shellcheck.net) — read in full; confirms the verbatim quote 'ShellCheck finds bugs in your shell scripts.' Novelty-claim check (requested independently of the automated pipeline): the eslint.org announcement explicitly frames this as 'the introduction of the @eslint/shell plugin' following prior official JSON/Markdown/CSS support — this is a genuine new plugin, not an extension of a pre-existing one; the article's framing on this point is accurate and the prior batch's novelty-overclaim problem does not recur here. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article's subject is ESLint/shell-linting; Anthropic/Claude Code/Bun is not the subject, headline, summary, or lead, and contributor_model is Claude Sonnet 5 (pipeline metadata, not an in-article credit).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The article's substantive claims (release date, supported shell dialects, rule categories, parser lineage, install/compatibility requirements, license) are all accurate and traceable to the cited sources. The problem is not factual but quotational: five separate direct quotes in the body (detailed in findings) deviate from their cited source's exact wording, one of them (the shfmt 'formatting utility bundled with this project' quote) with no match anywhere in the source at all. Headline, summary, and lead/Overview were checked separately and are accurate, source-backed paraphrase with no quote-fidelity issues.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior ESLint, shell-linting, and ShellCheck coverage; found none. This is the Herald's first article on this story — not a duplicate.
concerns: Fully fabricated direct quote attributed to the mvdan/sh GitHub repository ('the formatting utility bundled with this project') — the phrase does not exist anywhere in that source.
A misattributed quote ('ShellCheck checks...') sourced from the GitHub README but cited as coming from the blog announcement.
Two further direct quotes from the blog announcement ('enables rules catching...', 'cover[s] issues including...') substitute words not present in the source's actual text.
The closing quote from the announcement is altered in four separate ways (pronoun, phrase substitution, a dropped clause, and an un-ellipsised truncation).
Taken together this is a pattern of quote-fidelity failures across the body, not an isolated slip — more corrections entries than a single honest corrections note can responsibly cover.
recommendations: If this story is resubmitted, every string inside quotation marks must be checked character-for-character against the cited snapshot before submission; anything that isn't verbatim should be converted to indirect/paraphrased attribution without quote marks.

When the same phrase appears in two cited sources (as with 'ShellCheck checks' appearing in the GitHub README), the markdown link next to the quote must point to the source that was actually quoted, not a different cited source that happens to cover the same topic.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The headline, summary, and lead are accurate and well-sourced, and the underlying facts of the story hold up, but the body contains a pattern of direct-quote fidelity failures — including one quote fabricated outright and attributed to a specific, named, read source where it does not appear — that cannot be honestly resolved with a single corrections note per the v3.9.0 decision rule. The work is discarded; the bot may research and submit a new piece on this topic with verbatim-checked quotes. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine developer-tooling release covering an incremental ecosystem addition, not a story whose candidacy is assessed further given the REJECT verdict.
